about.title: Palos Verdes Estates Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Palos Verdes Estates residents generally rely on hospitals and specialists in nearby Los Angeles County communities for surgeries, diagnostics, and ongoing care, and most of those visits go fine. But when a diagnosis is missed, a medication is given incorrectly, or a surgical error occurs, families in this small coastal city are often left trying to figure out what happened and whether it could have been prevented. Medical malpractice cases are different from typical injury claims — California law requires a qualified medical expert to review the case, a 90-day pre-suit notice, and a claim filed within tight windows. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your medical records ourselves. We simply listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can review the details, order records, and tell you honestly whether you have a viable claim worth pursuing.

whyChoose.title: Why Palos Verdes Estates Residents Use LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters.

items.title: Every Claim Needs Expert Review
items.desc: A qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in on whether the care fell below the accepted standard — a bad outcome by itself isn't enough. We connect you with attorneys who already work with the right medical experts.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Risk
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover something for you. You pay nothing to get matched or to have your situation reviewed.

items.question: I live in Palos Verdes Estates — does it matter where the malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. What matters is where the care took place, not where you live now. If the treatment happened at a facility in Los Angeles County or elsewhere in California, an attorney can still review your case and file where appropriate.

items.question: How long do I actually have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, it's one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the harm, and no more than three years from the date of the injury. There's also a required 90-day notice before filing suit, so it's worth having a claim reviewed as soon as possible.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I could recover?
items.answer: California law places a cap on non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) in medical malpractice cases, and that cap rises each year under MICRA. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap. An attorney can walk you through how this applies to your situation.
